assessment: protected_catalog_copies performs its final active owner.require_current(), then removes owner from _LIVE in finally. The surrounding bounded_role_observation subsequently performs its own original-input currentness check and revokes/restores the read scope.

The latter reads are legitimate read-scope teardown after protection revocation. They do not return or retain an effect admission, and an ended protection object cannot be used to justify later effects.
The exact approved protection guarantee concerns the last active preflight observed-span close. It does not assert stage freshness through the later read-scope teardown or at context-manager return.
The actual stage factory remains a distinct live owner and revalidates on subsequent supported use. A detached inspect result or successful preflight exit is not a freshness or ownership capability.
Therefore a trailing stage native close after the bounded scope exits is not required for this explicitly read-only/no-retained-admission contract. The earlier approval remains unchanged.
future_contract_requirements: If a later API promises stage freshness through every normal-exit tail read, it must add an appropriate trailing stage close after those reads; the current approval does not establish that stronger promise.

Any future publication or stage-to-effect receiver must perform explicit actual-owner transfer and revalidation at its own effect boundary. It must not infer authority or freshness from the revoked preflight or saved descriptive record.

A later operation that intentionally changes original project inputs also needs explicit receiver/phase semantics rather than ignoring read-scope teardown failures or silently adopting the changed bytes.
